item1.justification: The trace misapplies §102 by treating toner as an “obvious variant” or as broadly encompassed rather than requiring every limitation to be disclosed in a single reference, and it also mixes §112(b) indefiniteness with §112(a) written-description analysis.

item2.justification: The conclusions repeatedly identify specific claim limitations—such as white or colored marking materials, toner, non-smooth surfaces, and scattering particles—and link them to US-2018113244-A1 or alleged specification deficiencies.

item3.justification: The office action says numerous dependent claims would be allowable if rewritten in independent form even though the same action separately concludes those claims are anticipated and obvious, creating an unexplained internal inconsistency.

item4.justification: The examiner’s high claim-breadth setting is reflected in expansive interpretations of scattering binders as white materials and toner as encompassed by generic printing-material disclosures, while the moderate strictness and combination threshold are consistent with rejection on predictable-substitution grounds.

item5.justification: The final rejection follows the earlier §103 and §112 rejection analyses and expressly relies on the cited reference, stated motivations, predictable results, and absence of secondary considerations.
